article_title: Supplemental Material for Important Text Characteristics for Early-Grades Text Complexity
citation: J. Fitzgerald et al. (2014). Important Text Characteristics for Early-Grades Text Complexity. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0037289
title: Corpus of 350 early-grades texts used for complexity measurement and prediction
description: The study's material base is a set of 350 early-grades texts, stratified by six categories and publisher-designated difficulty level for sampling. The 350 texts were digitized (including images) for teacher comparison, all 350 were assigned teacher-judgment logit scores and 0–100 complexity measures, and a random stratified sample of 90 texts (89 analyzed) was read by students. Text characteristics were computer- operationalized for these texts as predictors on the text-complexity outcome measure.
requirements: Texts must be digitizable, including images, for side-by-side computer-screen comparison by teachers
constraints: Student maze testing sampled only a subset of 90 texts from the 350, so student-based logits exist for fewer texts than teacher-based logits
target_learning_goals: Measuring and predicting early-reader text-complexity level
examples: A random sample of 90 texts was selected stratified by the six categories and by publisher-designated difficulty level; one passage was later rejected due to a printing error
key_sources: J. Fitzgerald et al. (2014). Important Text Characteristics for Early-Grades Text Complexity. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0037289
